title: Discontinuance Decision No. 1150/2022
text:
GE. 
Committee against Torture 
 
 Decision adopted by the Committee under article 22 of the 
Convention, concerning communication No. 1150/2022*, ** 
Communication submitted by: 
H. H. (represented by counsel Mr. Niels-Erik 
Hansen) 
Alleged victim: 
The complainant 
State party: 
Denmark 
Date of complaint: 
15 August 2022 (initial submission) 
Substantive issue: 
Deportation to Afghanistan; risk of torture 
 
1. The communication was submitted by Mr. H. H., an Afghan national. He alleges that his 
deportation would amount to a violation by the State Party of his rights under articles 3 
of the Convention. He requests the Committee to grant his request for interim measures 
to prevent the risk of irreparable harm he would face if deported to Afghanistan, due to 
his conversion to Christianity and the past difficulties his family has experienced with 
the Taliban. He is represented by counsel. 
2. On 19 August 2022, the communication was registered and the request for interim 
measures was granted. The State Party was requested to refrain from deporting Mr. H.H. 
to Afghanistan while his communication was under consideration by the Committee. 
3. On 19 August 2022, the State party was requested to provide the observations on both 
the admissibility and the merits of the complainant’s allegations no later than 20 February 
2023. On 31 January 2023, the State Party submitted the Danish Refugee Appals Board 
on 4 January decided to grant the complainant a residence permit and requested to 
discontinue the case. 
4. On 22 February 2023, the complainant was requested to submit his comments on the 
State party’s request for discontinuance no later than 22 March 2023. On 14 May 2024, 
the complainant was sent a final reminder to submit his comments on the State party’s 
request no later than 15 July 2024. No submissions have been received. 
5. At its meeting on 17 April 2026, in view of the fact that the complainant was granted a 
residence permit and did not submit his comments, and the Committee had no further
